questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance behind the vehicle in front of you. The other vehicle might back up suddenly. You also need space to move away from a vehicle coming toward you from behind.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press the right handgrip.
Press the left handgrip.
Press both handgrips at the same time.
Not press either handgrip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You will notice the problem by how the motorcycle handles instead.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to road conditions ahead.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders who have operated the involved motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have operated the involved motorcycle for less than six months.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind and rain while riding. Take a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you will feel tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would normally.
Start slowing earlier than you would normally.
Increase your following distance.
Not communicate with the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not communicate with the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: With a passenger on board, your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always tell your passenger about conditions ahead.

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The rider in back
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace. This ensures no riders are left behind.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase this to at least three seconds in poor conditions.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies even braking for both the front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Learns and remembers the approximate braking force used by the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies partial front braking whenever the rear brake is activated. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When preparing a passenger to ride, which instruction should you NOT give?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to mount after the engine starts. They should sit forward (close to you) and hold the passenger handholds or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: What about the oily strip in the center of a lane?

options.text: Is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane do not have the oily strip.
Adds to traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, it provides enough traction for motorcycles. Since the strip is usually about two feet wide, you can ride to one side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride in a side-by-side formation.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups should switch from staggered formation to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The portion of the lane nearest the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to experience a wind blast from the passing vehicle on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Other drivers have difficulty seeing motorcycles at night. What should you do?

options.text: Reduce their speed when riding at night.
Sound their horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights when riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Ride safely at night by reducing speed, increasing following distance, using the lights of vehicles ahead to see farther, using your high beam headlight when safe, and adjusting your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when the rider downshifts.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. It applies braking pressure to both when either lever is used. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: Passing another vehicle.
You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps others notice when you are slowing down more quickly than expected.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver in the lane next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead of them.
A parked car has a person in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing someone who is in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn when passing a vehicle or pedestrian that might move into your lane. If a driver is too close to the vehicle ahead, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. Sound your horn if you see someone in a parked car or a pedestrian or bicyclist in the street.

questions.question: When choosing where to position yourself in a lane, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change your position based on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on the situation.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. You can use any part of the lane. Choose the position where other drivers can see you best and where you have the most space around you.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: When riding, sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to help balance.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually stronger than a car's headlights.
Usually as strong as a car's headlights.
Usually weaker than a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually weaker than a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and weaker than car headlights.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.
